MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 18, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:01
p.m., on May 18, 2009, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 15, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  Council Member Ledesma

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury

INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht

CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he would like to continue item CS3 due to
  Council Member Ledesma's absence this evening.

City Council Minutes  1  May 18, 2009
 CS1. Labor Negotiations -- The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.
CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v.
  CUSD, Case No. 00207543.
CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel -- Initiation of Litigation. Pursuant to Subdivision
  (c) of Government Code Section 54956.9. Two Cases Under Consideration.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The Council
reconvened at 6:04 p.m. with four City Council Members present (Council Member Ledesma
was absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff for items CS1
and CS2 but there was no reportable action. Item CS3 was continued to the next City Council
meeting.

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

15.  Waste Disposal Agreement between the County of Orange and the City of Mission
  Viejo

  Senior Management Analyst Denise Matson presented the staff report.

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to continue this
  item for two weeks and direct staff to return with more detailed financial information,
  cost recovery data from the County, and answers to the following questions: (1) why is
  the County asking for an increase now; (2) what would the rate be today if CPI had been
  applied to our previous rate over the last twelve years; (3) what are other Orange County
  cities doing in terms of approval of this agreement, and (4) why would we be subject to
  higher rates if we do not execute the agreement by July 23, 2009.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ledesma

City Council Minutes  5  May 18, 2009
 Council Member Schlicht requested that items 18, 20, 21, 22, and 24 be considered together.

Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to approve items 18, 20,

PUBLIC HEARINGS

25.  Participation in the Orange County Sheriff’s Department False Alarm Fee Program

  At the hour of 6:34 p.m., Mayor Ury opened the public hearing.

  With no requests to speak, Mayor Ury closed the public hearing at 6:36 p.m.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report and Lt. Mike Gavin answered
  questions of the City Council.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, to
  adopt Resolution 09-16 Establishing a Fee for Responding To The Third And Subsequent
  False Alarms Within a Calendar Year, or an Intentionally Set False Alarm, in the Amount
  of $85.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  Ledesma

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

26.  Report from the Community of Character Committee Regarding "Rachel’s
  Challenge"

City Council Minutes  7  May 18, 2009
   Community Services Supervisor Virginia Chavez presented the report on behalf of the
  Community of Character Committee.

27.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

28.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that he was unable to attend the last meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA but he will provide a copy of the Minutes to the City Council
  Members for their information.

29.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Due to Council Member Ledesma’s absence, there was no report.

30.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

31.  Roundabout Intersections Committee Report

  Paul Riis, M.V.: read a statement on behalf of Bob Bruchmann who could not attend the
  meeting. Mr. Bruchmann does not support the Committee’s recommendation of a
  roundabout at Oso and Marguerite and stated that the Committee is pursuing a situation
  that is not in the best interests of the residents of Mission Viejo.

  Council Member Schlicht presented the report and stated that she recommends
  authorizing Scott Ritchie to create a conceptual drawing for the feasibility of a
  roundabout at Oso and Marguerite at the cost of $17,000.

  Simon Hartigan, M.V.: stated that Mission Viejo is home to some of the most heavily
  traveled intersections in the country. He finds it interesting that the City recommends
  adding more lanes at Oso and Marguerite and perhaps we can encourage less congestion
  with a roundabout at that location.

City Manager's Report

City Council Minutes  8  May 18, 2009
 City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

32.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

33.  La Paja Lane

  The following expressed concern and frustration with the ongoing construction at 26992
  La Paja Lane: Roberto Saracino, M.V.; Christine Saracino, M.V.; Stuart Jasper, M.V.;
  Catherine Jasper, M.V.; Jim Cantarella, M.V.; and Terry Yapp, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of the homeowner and Mr. Bonano presented a calendar
  for completion of the construction at 26992 La Paja: Kevin Dumont, Dumont
  Engineering, Architect of record, Rancho Santa Margarita; and Greg Bonano, project
  Contractor, M.V.

  Motion was made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, (1) direct staff to
  help seek a mutual agreement between the neighbors; (2) direct the City Attorney to
  concurrently prepare, for Closed Session, an analysis of the scope, nature, and timing of
  the legal remedies available to the City arising from the facts and circumstances related to
  the ongoing construction at 26992 La Paja Lane; and (3) in an effort to prepare for all
  potential circumstances, direct the City Attorney to prepare information for the June 1,
  2009, closed session, including an analysis of the legality of the work that has been
  completed on the property as well as planned future work on the property and an analysis
  of the City’s legal enforcement options, with estimated timeframes for action.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ledesma

Council Member Kelley acknowledged the Mission Viejo/Saddleback Valley Elks Lodge for
donating 4,400 dictionaries to all of the third grade students in Saddleback Valley. She

City Council Minutes  9  May 18, 2009
 announced that this is the third year that the Elk’s have made this very generous donation and, in
addition, they have recently awarded several scholarships to graduating seniors. She stated that
we appreciate the work the Elk’s do to help make our community better, especially as advocates
for our young people. Council Member Kelley announced that the City has been recognized as a
“Shining Star” by the Saddleback Valley Prevention Coalition in recognition of the work the
Council undertook to make Mission Viejo the first city in Orange County to adopt a Social Host
Ordinance. Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at the recent parenting workshop,
Building a Nation of Character, which was hosted by the Community of Character and presented
by Russell Williams of The Passkeys Foundation. The workshop will be televised on Mission
Viejo Television and it’s a wonderful tool for the difficult job of parenting our children. She
encouraged residents to attend the 20th Annual KSBR Birthday Bash on May 24, 2009, on the
Village Green at the Murray Community Center and the City’s Memorial Day recognition
ceremony on May 25th at 8:30 a.m. at the Veteran’s Memorial Plaza near the Community
Center. Council Member Kelley also reminded residents to be sure to vote tomorrow and she
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of May is moral courage.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that earlier this evening she attended the Tea Party at the
corner of La Paz and Marguerite. She encouraged residents to vote tomorrow and she
acknowledged that she hopes the electorate votes no. Council Member Schlicht stated that it is
fiscally irresponsible to extend and amend maintenance contracts that are two years old. In this
market it’s smarter to go out to bid to try and find a better price. She stated that the only way the
Council can direct staff to go out to bid is here in an open forum and that the City should be a
little bit more responsive to tax dollars. Council Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at
the recent Orange County Islamic Foundation luncheon to honor retired Chief of Police Lt. Steve
Bernardi and to welcome Mission Viejo’s new Chief, Lt. Mike Gavin.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that the Council needs to do a better job focusing on the issues.
Inflammatory comments about residents and irresponsible spending should be left at the door.
He outlined the various expenditures that the Council has made which are going to return to the
community the quality of life that the residents expect. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that the
Council Members, himself included, should be talking about issues not personalities and he
encouraged all of his colleagues to keep that in mind. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that they
attempt to find the best solution for every situation and at the end of a discussion, the Council

City Council Minutes  10  May 18, 2009
 votes to decide what happens. Council Members won’t always agree but they always get a
majority to move forward in a particular direction.

Mayor Ury

34.  Public Input to Budget Deliberations

  Motion was made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to direct staff to
  (1) televise all upcoming budget meetings; and (2) create an email address
  (budget@cityofmissionviejo.org) for public input to the budget process, to be distributed
  to all five City Council Members, the City Manager, and the Director of Administrative
  Services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
  AYES:  Kelley, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  Ledesma

Mayor Ury stated that words are important and they are to be taken very seriously, especially
when someone is making accusations. He attempted to clarify his prior comments regarding a
Council Member’s job to go through the process of learning a role, conducting research, and
being prepared to move forward in a timely fashion. He stated that it is incumbent upon all of
the Council Members to know their job and walk in prepared, yet he is not sure that the level of
preparedness with others is where it needs to be. Mayor Ury reminded everyone of the
Memorial Day ceremony on Monday, May 25th at 8:30 a.m. at the Community Center.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:36 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, June 1, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

Karen Hamman, City Clerk
